judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on House Bill 193, a gun bill. It lets staff at private schools carry a gun at school if the school agrees in writing. It also lets permit holders carry a hidden handgun in a church that shares land with a school. It also raised the penalties for attacking or threatening a public official. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The House voted 72-48 to override, the Senate did the same that day, and the bill became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on House Bill 318, an immigration bill. Jails must check the status of anyone charged with a felony, some serious misdemeanors, or drunk driving. If federal agents want the person, the jail must hold them up to 48 more hours after they would have gone free. Judges must run the same check when they set bail. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The House voted 72-48 to override, the Senate did the same that day, and the bill became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on House Bill 805. It sets one fixed meaning of sex, man and woman for every state and local rule, and it stops state money from paying for gender transition care in prisons. The same law makes porn sites check the age and written consent of everyone in an image, and take images down within 72 hours when asked. It also changed school rules on shared sleeping quarters and library books. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The House voted 72-48 to override, the Senate did the same that day, and the bill became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on Senate Bill 266, an energy bill. It erased the rule that big power companies must cut carbon dioxide 70 percent below 2005 levels by 2030. The 2050 goal of no net emissions stays. The law also lets a power company raise rates to pay for a plant that is still being built. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The Senate voted 30-18 to override, the House did the same that day, and the bill became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on Senate Bill 153, the Border Protection Act. State police and prison agencies must sign deals to work with federal immigration agents. State agencies must also stop giving state-paid benefits and housing help to people here without legal permission, though food aid is left alone. A city or county with a sanctuary policy can now be sued. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The Senate voted 30-19 to override in July 2025, the House followed in June 2026, and the bill became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes on Senate Bill 227. Public schools may no longer run a diversity, equity and inclusion office, or teach what the law calls divisive concepts. One banned idea is that one race or sex is better than another. Free speech and normal history teaching are protected. Each school must report every year that it follows the law. A yes vote backed making the bill law over the governor's veto. The Senate voted 30-19 to override in July 2025, the House followed in June 2026, and the bill became law.

State universities and community colleges may no longer keep a diversity, equity and inclusion office, or employ staff to promote what the law calls divisive concepts.
